channel.title: RFI - All the news from France, Europe, Africa and the rest of the world.
channel.description: Follow any political information, cultural, sporting and live streaming on RFI. The latest information, news and events around the world.

item.title: Paris suburb shooting suspect 'targeted Muslims, Africans or North Africans'
item.description: The man being held over the shootings which took place last Friday in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière – which left one man dead and several people wounded, including an 11-year-old girl – has said he specifically targeted people of Muslim, African or North African appearance, anti-terrorism investigators revealed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Paul Myers

item.title: Real Madrid says Mbappé was wrong over Mao Zedong as China fallout continues
item.description: Spanish football club Real Madrid, as well as Spanish league bosses, were on Thursday waiting to see if their apologies had led to a thaw in relations with China following striker Kylian Mbappé's comments about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
item.dc:creator: Paul Myers

item.title: US judge narrows Macrons' defamation lawsuit against American podcaster
item.description: A judge in the United States has ruled that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte ​could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of the American podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Spain begins three days of national mourning after train crash kills at least 68
item.description: Spain on Thursday began three days of official mourning, after a rail collision south of Madrid on Wednesday killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100.
item.dc:creator: Paul Myers

item.title: Russia-Africa summit tests Moscow's ambitions for broader influence
item.description: More than 20 African leaders are in Moscow for a summit that will test Russia's bid to expand its influence on the continent. The two-day Russia-Africa Summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy sanctions over its Ukraine offensive – and as several African governments turn to it for security assistance.
item.source: © Ivan Sekretarev/Russia-Africa Summit host photo agency via AP
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Medical experts warn climate change is now a 'global health emergency'
item.description: The damage wreaked by climate change on human health is escalating, experts warn, with deaths from heat, drought and other extreme weather rising faster than the world is taking action to limit global warming. Published on Wednesday, a report by medical journal The Lancet calls for climate change to be declared "a global health emergency".
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: French Senate toughens proposals to make rioters pay for damage
item.description: The upper house of the French parliament has toughened a proposed law that would make people who participate in rioting and vandalism liable for up to €10,000, after nationwide protests against failing schools and the cost of living that turned violent in Paris and other cities. Rights groups warn the legislation could undermine the democratic right to protest.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Egypt's mahrganat music: from the streets to five-star hotels
item.description: Born in Egypt’s working-class neighbourhoods, mahraganat music is loud and raw, and these days it is practically impossible to escape. But for the artists behind it, mahraganat is more than just party music: they see it as the latest chapter in Egypt’s rich musical history.
item.dc:creator: Anne-Marie Bissada

item.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
item.description: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival's opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel's pivotal general election.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: French media protest manhandling of journalists at far-right party rally
item.description: More than 40 French media groups, including Radio France International, have called on Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally (RN) to allow them to work freely after journalists were allegedly subjected to rough treatment at a party congress last weekend.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Iraqi court jails seven French nationals over Islamic State membership
item.description: An Iraqi court has sentenced seven French nationals to prison for belonging to the Islamic State armed group, handing down the first verdicts in proceedings involving French detainees transferred from Syria last year.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Somalia reports deadly fighting with Al-Shabaab as both sides claim heavy losses
item.description: Somalia’s government and Al-Shabaab militants have issued sharply conflicting accounts of deadly fighting near the southern city of Leego, with both sides claiming to have inflicted heavy losses during a battle on Monday.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: PSG bosses hail club of the year success at 2026 Ballon d'Or awards
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaïfi on Tuesday praised head coach Luis Enrique and his squad after the club retained the Ballon d’Or Club of the Year award.
item.dc:creator: Paul Myers

item.title: France pledges university admissions overhaul and education funding to ease protests
item.description: France’s government has promised to replace Parcoursup, the university admissions platform, and to invest in schools and student support, offering a package of concessions aimed at defusing weeks of protests over education and the rising cost of living.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Polls open in Israel as Netanyahu faces close contest after three years of war
item.description: Polls opened in Israel on Tuesday in the country’s first election since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a close contest after three years of war and deepening political divisions.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Macron vows to stand firm against disorder during visit to Marseille
item.description: President Emmanuel Macron on Monday gave his full support to security forces as France prepared for a third consecutive weekend of protests over the poor state of schools and the rising cost of living.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Putellas and Kane win 2026 Ballon d'Or as PSG retain men's team of year prize
item.description: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas and the Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the 2026 women's and men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night as Paris Saint-Germain retained the men's team of the year award.
item.source: Action Images via Reuters - Matthew Childs
item.dc:creator: Paul Myers

item.title: Senegal PM vows to address economic issues as 2026 Youth Olympics Games loom
item.description: Senegal's Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo on Monday promised to solve the battle over the budget between members of the ruling Pastef party as the country counts down for the start of the 2026 Youth Olympic games on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Paul Myers

item.title: Le Pen widens poll lead as Mélenchon closes in on run-off spot
item.description: Former French prime minister Édouard Philippe would finish only third in the first round of the presidential election, behind Jean-Luc Mélenchon, according to a new Cluster 17 poll for Politico published on Monday.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Serbia's student movement ousts longtime leader Vucic
item.description: Serbia's student-led movement was on Monday enjoying its first day of power after ending the 14-year reign of Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: Macron leads congratulations to Lula over election victory in Brazil
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron was among the world leaders on Monday to hail Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's re-election as Brazil's president.
item.dc:creator: RFI

item.title: French unions and protest groups call fresh rallies and nationwide strike
item.description: French unions and protest groups have called for fresh demonstrations on 31 October and a nationwide strike on 5 November, seeking to build on a movement over wages, living costs and public services after a massive police deployment helped contain unrest during Saturday’s marches.
item.dc:creator: RFI
